transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (CTO - Marigold), Maya Patel (Infra), Raj Singh (Security), Tina Gomez (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining. this is jordan lee from redwood, joining with priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alex: good thanks, alex here. gonna keep this pretty pragmatic our infra folks are on the call to talk network and security.
[00:13] Maya: hi yes maya, i'll be the point for VPCs.
[00:16] Raj: raj here, security questions up front, so apologies if i interrupt.
[00:20] Jordan: totally, that's what we're here for. quick agenda — private deployment options, network patterns (peering, transit gateway, private endpoints), region gating constraints for our EU/APAC customers, and any compliance asks. then next steps. sound ok?
[00:33] Tina: yep sounds good.

[02:10] Priya: to start, our Private offering gives you a customer-controlled VPC peered or connected to our control plane via private endpoints. for aws we usually recommend interface endpoints for the control plane and transit gateway for higher scale, but cross-account peering is also supported for smaller setups.
[02:32] Alex: when you say "control plane" — is that still reachable over the public internet or is it all private?
[02:37] Priya: good question. we have both flavors. for full isolation we do a private-control-plane mode where traffic goes over our private endpoints (interface endpoints) and the control plane sits in your VPC or private connectivity via a customer-managed peering. some customers choose dedicated-hosted where control plane traffic is over a managed private link.
[02:58] Maya: are there NAT or egress requirements? our compliance team wants egress to go through our inspection boxes only.
[03:05] Priya: yes you can force egress through your NAT/inspection. typically with transit gateway you advertise routes and we respect the next-hop — so traffic destined for our inference nodes can go via the transit and then out through your inspection. we also support static routes via VPC peering but that doesn't propagate routes to a transit gateway automatically — you might need route rules on the peering.

[06:20] Raj: on the compliance side, we need to understand where logs live, how KMS is used for keys, and whether we can use our HSM. we also need SOC2 and ISO artifact checklist.
[06:35] Jordan: totally. we can provide SOC2/ISO packages and an HSM/KMS integration guide. we support customer-managed keys via KMS, and for on-prem HSMs we have integrations for the private package — it's not plug-and-play but we've done it with a few banks. i'll share the compliance pack after the call.

[08:45] Alex: region gating — we have data residency rules for EU and also some APAC partners where inference must stay in-region. how does Redwood handle multi-region private deployments?
[08:55] Priya: you can pin model versions to region-specific queues. for private you can deploy nodes in multiple regions and the control plane will route to the nearest region by policy. there is also an option to restrict routing only to specific regions — we call that region gating — where the policy denies egress to non-approved regions. latency-wise, local region nodes are preferred; fallback to another region is only if you opt-in for cross-region resilience.
[09:20] Maya: if we need to keep inference inside eu-west-1, can we prevent accidental failover to us-east-1?
[09:26] Priya: yes, you can set routing policies to strict region-only. default is to allow fallback for availability, but strict mode keeps traffic in-region and surfaces capacity errors instead of failing over.

[11:55] Tina: cost is a concern — we have a small ML team and don't want sky-high bills. how different is Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted on cost basis?
[12:05] Jordan: hosted is usual pay-as-you-go; private with shared-hosted control plane has a similar consumption model plus private networking costs. dedicated/reserved capacity is most predictable but requires a commit. typically banks choose dedicated for SLAs; startups might start on private and move to dedicated as load grows. priya has some details on batching and cache to reduce per-token costs.
[12:30] Priya: yes, two levers: batching (we can do continuous batching patterns tuned to your latency SLO) and prefix/KV cache — sorry sometimes the speech system writes KV "cash" — but the point is we cache common prefixes. that can drop token counts substantially for repeated customer prompts.

[15:02] Alex: about peering — we're heavy users of transit gateway. does Redwood support TGW attachment and route propagation?
[15:10] Priya: yes we support TGW attachments. we typically suggest a one-way advertisement pattern: customer attaches TGW and advertises the private subnet containing the endpoints. Redwood's peering endpoint will accept routes and we request a clear route map. for cross-account setups we can do DMZ VPCs and then attach to TGW as well.
[15:33] Maya: what about cross-region peering costs? our finance team cares.
[15:39] Jordan: there are cross-region data transfer costs from cloud provider plus any transit gateway inter-region charges. we'll provide estimates in the workbook.

[18:48] Raj: encryption in flight and at rest — are you using TLS? where are keys stored?
[18:55] Priya: everything in flight is TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS for control plane when using private endpoints. at rest we encrypt with customer-managed KMS keys if you choose that option. for HSM we have integrations but there may be added ops work.

[21:15] Alex: for the private endpoints, do customers need to expose route tables to accept interface endpoints? how are security groups handled?
[21:24] Priya: interface endpoints require ENIs in subnets and security groups. you control the SG rules. we give a minimal list: allow outbound to Redwood control-plane IPs and allow the ENIs to initiate. route tables should have access to your outbound inspection if you require egress.

[24:02] Tina: who usually owns the rollout internally? product, infra, security?
[24:09] Jordan: it's cross-functional. usually infra kicks off the network setup, security validates compliance artifacts, and product owns acceptance criteria and prompt/regression tests. for the pilot we recommend a two-week network setup and a four-week evaluation with a small traffic profile.

[26:35] Maya: we also have some legacy on-prem racks that need to talk to the model endpoint from a private datacenter. is there an on-prem option?
[26:44] Priya: yes, we have a private on-prem package that installs the inference dataplane inside your environment and connects a private control plane. that's more involved — audits, air-gap considerations — but possible. many customers prefer the VPC/private endpoints first, then later consider on-prem if needed.

[29:01] Raj: about audit logs — we need detailed request/response metadata for compliance. can we retain logs for 7 years?
[29:10] Jordan: retention policies are configurable. long-term retention may be an add-on because of storage costs, but we can export logs to your S3 or SIEM and you can own the retention. we'll share the logging spec.

[32:40] Alex: what's your typical pilot success criteria?
[32:47] Priya: throughput/latency within agreed SLOs, secure connectivity validated (private endpoints and egress inspection), and quality baseline on our eval prompts — no regressions. we also look at cost per token and caching benefits.

[35:12] Tina: timeline — we're hoping to have something in prod in Q4 but network team needs to approve.
[35:20] Jordan: that sounds doable. pilot in September/October could hit Q4 if approvals move quickly.

[38:00] Maya: question about SSO — we use SAML SSO and RBAC needs mapping to our teams.
[38:08] Priya: we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based and can be integrated with your IdP; we can map groups to roles.

[41:30] Raj: also want to note PDPO / local regulations for APAC — any known restrictions in say singapore or japan you run into?
[41:38] Priya: the main restriction is residency and sometimes export controls depending on model weights. for our private offering we can pin nodes to those regions; for some models there are license constraints. we'll flag any model-specific export constraints in the workbook.

[44:00] Jordan: ok quick recap — we'll send the private deployment workbook + pricing, schedule a deep network session with maya and raj, and priya will prepare a logging/compliance spec. action items we'll list in the notes.
[44:18] Alex: thanks, appreciate it.
[44:21] Maya: thanks everyone — i'll circulate VPC diagrams.
[44:25] Raj: i'll compile compliance artifact list.
[44:28] Jordan: great — we'll follow up by Wednesday. thanks all.
